arxiv-2112-06485.title: Wigner-Weyl description of light absorption in disordered semiconductor alloys using the localization landscape theory
arxiv-2112-06485.creator: Jean-Philippe Banon, Pierre Pelletier, Claude Weisbuch, Svitlana Mayboroda, Marcel Filoche
arxiv-2112-06485.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jean-Philippe Banon, Pierre Pelletier, Claude Weisbuch, Svitlana Mayboroda, Marcel Filoche. The presence of disorder in semiconductors can dramatically change their physical properties. Yet, models faithfully accounting for it are still scarce and computationally inefficient. We present a mathematical and computational model able to simulate the optoelectronic response of semiconductor alloys of several tens of nanometer sidelength, while at the same time accounting for the quantum localization effects induced by the compositional disorder at the nano-scale.

In this work we study electromagnetic properties of a resonator recently suggested for the search of axions — a hypothetical candidate to explain dark matter. A wire medium loaded resonator (called a plasma haloscope when used to search for dark matter) consists of a box filled with a dense array of parallel wires electrically connected to top and bottom walls.

arxiv-2305-10480.title: ALMA and Keck analysis of Fomalhaut field sources: JWST’s Great Dust Cloud is a background object 2023 ALMA and Keck analysis of Fomalhaut field sources: JWST’s Great Dust Cloud is a background object – References
arxiv-2305-10480.creator: Grant M. Kennedy, Joshua B. Lovell, Paul Kalas & Michael P. Fitzgerald
arxiv-2305-10480.description: Abstract At 7.7 pc, the A-type star Fomalhaut hosts a bright debris disk with multiple radial components. The disk is eccentric and misaligned, strongly suggesting that it is sculpted by interaction with one or more planets. Compact sources are now being detected with JWST, suggesting that new planet detections may be imminent.

arxiv-2404-11805.title: Covariant operator formalism for higher derivative systems: Vector spin- 0 0 dual model as a prelude to generalized QED 4
arxiv-2404-11805.creator: G. B. de Gracia, A. A. Nogueira
arxiv-2404-11805.description: Abstract In this work we extend the Kugo-Ojima-Nakanishi covariant operator formalism to quantize two higher derivative systems, considering their extended phase space structures. More specifically, the one describing spin- 0 0 particles by a vector field and the generalized electrodynamics. We investigate the commutator structure of these theories and present the definition of their physical Hilbert subspaces.

arxiv-2404-15180.title: Does anti-Unruh effect assist quantum entanglement and coherence?
arxiv-2404-15180.creator: Shu-Min Wu 1 , Xiao-Wei Teng 1 , Jin-Xuan Li 1 , Hao-Sheng Zeng 2 , Tonghua Liu 3
arxiv-2404-15180.description: Abstract In this paper, we use the concepts of quantum entanglement and coherence to analyze the Unruh and anti-Unruh effects based on the model of Unruh-DeWitt detector. For the first time, we find that (i) the Unruh effect reduces quantum entanglement but enhances quantum coherence; (ii) the anti-Unruh effect enhances quantum entanglement but reduces quantum coherence.

arxiv-2502-11510.creator: Tess O’Brien, Matthew T. Moores, David Warton, Daniel Falster
arxiv-2502-11510.description: Abstract Longitudinal models with dynamics governed by differential equations may require numerical integration alongside parameter estimation. We have identified a situation where the numerical integration introduces error in such a way that it becomes a novel source of non-uniqueness in estimation.

arxiv-2602-23390.title: Pacing Opinion Polarization via Graph Reinforcement Learning Thanks: Citation : Authors. Title. Pages…. DOI:000000/11111.
arxiv-2602-23390.creator: Mingkai Liao
arxiv-2602-23390.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mingkai Liao. Opinion polarization in online social networks poses a critical challenge to social cohesion and democratic processes. Recent work formulates polarization moderation as algorithmic intervention problems under opinion dynamics models, most notably the Friedkin–Johnsen (FJ) model. However, existing approaches are largely tailored to specific linear settings and rely on closed-form steady-state analysis, limiting their scalability, adaptability, and applicability to cost-aware, nonlinear, or topology-altering interventions. In this paper, we propose PACIFIER , a graph reinforcement learning framework for sequential polarization moderation via network interventions.
